title: unified-rollouts: enhanced weighted canary + shadow/A-B auto-rollback (multi-metric)
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds weighted canary + shadow/A-B auto-rollback policy; configurable multi-metric thresholds and cooldown windows. No API surface breaking changes. Backward compatible rollout configs continue to work.
description: Motivation: customers running large-scale model rollouts requested more flexible canary behaviors: weighted canaries (gradual traffic splits), combined shadow and A/B experiments, and automated rollback driven by multiple metrics (latency, error rate, quality regressions). This PR extends the unified-rollouts subsystem to support weighted canary profiles, shadow+A/B routing combinations, and a multi-metric auto-rollback engine with configurable aggregation windows. Summary of changes: 1) rollout model and controller: add WeightedCanaryProfile with traffic weights, decay/cooldown rules, and priority ordering for shadow vs active variants. 2) auto-rollback: implement MultiMetricEvaluator that computes windowed signals (p95 latency, 5xx rate, delta-quality) and evaluates compound rules (AND/OR) with hysteresis to avoid flapping. 3) routing: extend smart-router to support weighted fanout and deterministic shadow copies for compatibility with cache/KV semantics. 4) API and config: new fields in rollout spec (weighted_steps, shadow_ratio, metrics_rules) with defaults preserving existing behavior. 5) telemetry: new rollout metrics and dashboards; rollout events now emit detailed reasons for rollouts/rollbacks. Backwards compatibility and safety: default configs keep previous canary behavior (single step, 100% or 0%). Auto-rollback is opt-in via metrics_rules; teams can enable progressive rollout strategies per model. Testing and validation: unit tests for evaluator logic, e2e canary simulation harness updates, staging canary against real traffic profile. Migration notes: existing rollout specs without weighted_steps are unaffected. Operators can migrate incrementally by adding weighted_steps entries. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-9421) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] e2e simulation harness updated - [x] observability dashboards updated - [x] rollout guide and examples updated (redwood-docs) See related work: ENG-9478 (shadow-ab experiments) and SUP-2109 (customer incident motivating hysteresis).

review_comments: Maya Thompson: Overall looks good. One concern: how do we ensure KV cache determinism when shadowing weighted traffic? Can we guarantee identical cache keys?
Priya Nair: We add deterministic hashing in weighted_router and an option to force-prefetch KV for shadowed requests. Added tests that assert KV key parity in router tests.
Ethan Li: The hysteresis window seems aggressive (30s). For high-throughput low-latency customers that could delay rollback. Suggest making cooldown configurable per rollout and default to 15s.
Priya Nair: Agreed. Made cooldown configurable with default 15s and documented tradeoffs in the design doc.
Sofia Ramirez: CI flakes on the e2e harness when simulating very high variance traffic. Please add retry logic and widen simulation variance bounds to reduce nondeterminism.
Priya Nair: Added retry/backoff in the harness and made the simulation seed deterministic for CI runs. Re-ran tests; green.
Maya Thompson: Approving — left a minor nit about a log message format. Not blocking.
Ethan Li: Approved after cooldown default change and test stabilization.
